title: Block vs inline content model
learningObjectives: Apply block vs inline content model accurately and accessibly.

understand.concept: Block and inline describe common layout behaviour, but modern HTML content categories and CSS display are more precise. Element validity depends on content models, not just visual display.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct HTML semantics improve accessibility, maintainability and browser interoperability.
understand.analogy: Think of a document where every section has a clear role.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is limited; exact behaviour follows HTML semantics and browser rules.

explain.narrative: Block and inline describe common layout behaviour, but modern HTML content categories and CSS display are more precise. Element validity depends on content models, not just visual display.

examples.explanation: Inspect the code, semantic roles, attributes and browser behaviour.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser renders the HTML structure.

practise.guidedTask: Modify the example and test with keyboard and browser inspection.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible semantic page section and explain your element choices.
hints: Use CSS for appearance without changing semantics.
Do not rely only on browser defaults for security or accessibility.

practice.starterCode: A paragraph contains important inline text.
practice.resetCode: A paragraph contains important inline text.

questions.prompt: Does CSS display alone decide whether HTML nesting is valid?
questions.explanation: Base decisions on semantic purpose, accessibility and browser behaviour.

questions.prompt: Does semantic HTML alone guarantee complete accessibility?
questions.explanation: Test keyboard access, labels, contrast and media alternatives.
